data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A test constrains its subject, rather than describing it, when the test is installed before the subject's behaviour is fixed and the installation ritual is shown to fail first. The 3-of-26 result reflects exactly this: only the mutations that were installed under a shown-to-fail-first discipline survived, and the 1-of-9 compile.py loss is the signature of an installation gate that was never actually exercised.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The 3-of-26 distribution could be explained by mutation difficulty rather than installation order if the surviving mutations were all in hard-to-reach code paths.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the compile.py mutation loss was due to an unrelated content-edit hole, then the shown-to-fail-first mechanism did not actually operate there.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"Single-author, single-repository, single-week confound means the observed pattern may reflect the author's habits rather than a general condition on tests.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"When a test is written against an already-working subject, it records the subject's current behaviour and is satisfied by construction; it describes. When the test is installed as a guard that is demonstrated to fail against a planted mutation before the subject is accepted, it binds a counterfactual: subject passes only if the guarded behaviour is present. The 1-of-9 compile.py loss shows the gap between describing an installation ritual and performing it: a guard that never fails on its author is not a guard.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
